items.claim: Snip preview ignores a tuned `snipPath` radius
Spiro deactivation leaves the snap trail session and pointer follower open

items.note: Warp Settings is now enabled only by a warp that still makes its shape. Expand Warp keeps the looser check on purpose (A's suggestion), because dropping a stale warp still changes the document.

items.claim: A warp tool attached to two canvases loses the first one
items.note: Each canvas now gets its own handle layer reading its own deps, and activating the tool redraws every attached canvas.
`warpSettingOf` now rejects non-finite numbers. The same gap was in `tolerance` (Infinity got through), and that is fixed in the same commit.

items.claim: A warp begun on text whose face is still loading never converts it
items.note: for the drag. The drag now keeps its grab and converts the text on the first move after the face loads. `OutlineSession` gained `waiting()`, and `outlineScene.ts` gained a `registerTestFont()` test helper. `pin.addPin`, the single-call case B also named, is unchanged: it is one immediate click and can't wait, so a click on still-loading text does nothing and the next click converts it.

items.claim: Switching away from the spiro tool leaves its cursor's snap session open and the pointer followed
configureWarp silently shrinks a cloth warp finer than 16×16 when any other setting changes
Snip's hover preview ignores `<SceneCanvas tune>` for `snipPath`, so it can show a different piece than the click cuts
planSnip rebuilds every mark's outline for every candidate stroke on each hover move (quadratic)
`configureWarp` and `expandWarp` count a stale warp as one the selection holds, while `configureWarp`'s run and form ignore it
A warp or pin begun while a selected text's face is still loading lays the fresh warp over the text but never converts it
A warp tool attached to two canvases loses the first canvas's scene when the second detaches
